sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Rauh Goddess Statues***, also referred to as ***Rauh Queen Statues*** and other names in the community, are objects in Elden Ring. All information about the statues and the unseen character they depict is conjectural, based on visual details and contextual clues.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.markdown: Statues of a mysterious woman with a great octagonal crown are prominently featured throughout the Ancient Ruins of Rauh, a land blessed by the primordial Crucible of life. Both the hornsent and Kindred of Rot offer their prayers to this goddess-like figure. The Verdigris Discus can be found under one of these statues. The [[item:antiquity-scholar-s-cookbook-2|Antiquity Scholar's Cookbook [2]]] and the Bondstone are located beneath another, held by the corpse of a hornsent. In addition, female figures with pointed headpieces and long side veils are represented in other artistic reliefs at the Rauh ruins.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Ranni's Followers*** is a faction loyal to Ranni the Witch in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
The followers were Ranni's innermost circle of vassals, each a champion sworn to serve their Lady. They formed on the Night of Black Knives to help her thwart her fate and walk the dark path of the Empyrean. Blaidd and Iji, her most trusted companions, were the first to join.

Ranni required the Fingerslayer Blade, the legendary treasure of Nokron, Eternal City, to advance her agenda. Her followers spent years searching for a path to the Eternal City, but the road remained inaccessible.

The group disbands when Ranni departs for the Moonlight Altar from Renna's Rise.

- Obtained from a corpse in southwestern Liurnia of the Lakes found lying on a stone ledge that juts out from a cliff, below the Malefactor's Evergaol.
- Obtained from a chest in central Altus Plateau, found within an enemy camp northwest of Altus Highway Junction.
- Obtained from Fia in the Roundtable Hold after speaking to her about Rogier.
- Obtained by killing Lesser Wormface enemies in central Altus Plateau, around the Minor Erdtree and in southern Crumbling Farum Azula, as a rare (2.5%) drop.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.markdown:
Prevents the loss of Runes upon death (except for deaths cause by Death Blight).

Breaks upon death (except for deaths caused by Death Blight).

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Useful to equip when you are about to run into an area full of dangerous enemies, just keep in mind to unequip afterwards so as to not lose it unnecessarily.
- Like the Twiggy Cracked Tear, since it prevents you from dropping a Bloodstain with your runes upon death it will also prevent it from replacing your previous one and therefore gives you another chance to grab it.
 - This is especially useful around large drops since it makes the consequences around fall damage deaths much smaller, provided you are willing to risk losing a twig.
- Be careful when farming these, as the only enemies that drop them are also some of a few that can inflict Death Blight and therefore circumvent the protective effect.
- Can be used to transport out a bunch of Runes stuck inside of a boss room, especially when combined with quitting out to the main menu to reset the character to just outside of the boss room's fog wall.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- The default skill is good for dealing with enemies that are blocking, though it can also be used by simply switching to an empty right-hand slot or replicated by continuously attacking if the blocker isn't using a greatshield.
- Has an entirely unique heavy attack chain consisting of only thrusts.
 - Since these attacks will reliably deal Pierce damage they pair well with the Spear Talisman for extra counter damage against attacking foes. Note that this works best with purely Physical infusions, as split Elemental damage (such as Magic or Lightning) will note benefit from the bonus to Pierce damage.
- Surprisingly decent for the Magic and Flame Art/Sacred affinities, placing it closer to the middle of the pack than the end for damage.
- When using its Keen affinity it actually has slightly weaker Dexterity-scaling for "bullet"-type (i.e. doesn't scale directly with the used weapon's damage) Skills with a Keen, Quality, Lightning, or Cold affinity, giving them usually about 2% less damage than they otherwise would have. This includes, as an example, the skills Beast's Roar, Storm Blade, Thunderbolt, and Hoarfrost Stomp (these skills however perform as normal on any affinity besides Keen).
- Consistently the third weakest weapon in the type in terms of pure Attack Power (AP), outclassing only the Weathered Straight Sword and Cane Sword.
- Quite short, the shortest of its weapon type in fact.
- Wielded by Foot Soldiers.

sections.heading: Upgrade Information
sections.markdown:
- Upgraded with regular Smithing Stones.
- Can have its Affinity and Skill changed.
- All non-physical Affinities lower all types of guarded damage negation by 5%, except for the associated element where the damage negation increases by 25% and another element also increases by 15%.
 - Magic negation receives the secondary 15% negation bonus on Sacred and Cold affinities, Fire negation gets the increase on Lightning affinity, Lightning negation gets the increase on Fire and Flame Art affinities, and Holy negation gets the increase on Magic affinity.
- The upper number in the Atk column denotes Physical base damage while the lower, colored number in the Atk column denotes elemental base damage: red for Fire damage, yellow for Lightning damage, orange for Holy damage, and cyan for Magic damage.
- See the Weapon Scaling page for what the scaling values mean.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Sites of Grace** () are special locations in Elden Ring. They serve as resting points where players can fast-travel and manage various aspects of their character. Resting at these locations has multiple effects and provides options to customize and progress.

sections.heading: Using Sites of Grace
sections.markdown:
Resting at a Site of Grace has the following effects**:
- Restores the player's HP and FP to full and removes all Buffs and Status Ailments
- Refills all charges for both Sacred Flasks
- Sets the Site of Grace as the player's respawn point
- Respawns Enemies killed throughout the game world (exceptions include Bosses, NPCs, and other foes)
- Displays the Site of Grace menu
The Site of Grace menu offers the following options**:

- Pass Time: Advance time to morning, noon, or nightfall.
- Level Up: Allocate Runes to improve character stats.
- Flasks
 - Add charge to flask
 - Increase amount replenished by flasks
 - Allocate flask charges
- Memorize Spell
- Mix Wondrous Physick
- Sort Chest
- Great Runes
- Ashes of War
- Alter Garments
- Leave

Special options at certain Graces:
- Talk to Melina
- Tell her you're off to Roundtable Hold
- Talk to Miniature Ranni
- Listen to the sound of flame

POWER: 75% SS

An exceptional spell for a fighter-mage hybrid character; it adds raw Magic damage to your equipped melee weapon. The Power ratio is the damage added to every base strike. This added damage is also completely independent to how high or low the base damage of the original weapon is, so a strong boost to a normally weak-but-fast weapon could have quite a significant DPS effect.

Also note, 2-handing the weapon after enchanting it does not appear to add the 50% damage multiplication to the magical part of the damage, only the base physical damage is affected.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: is an NPC and boss in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Gideon Ofnir is the Tarnished leader of Roundtable Hold and the adoptive father of Nepheli Loux. Called to the Lands Between by the guidance of Grace, Gideon wishes to become Elden Lord. To this end he accumulates information on the Shardbearers, employing a network of spies to aid in his hunt for knowledge. Initially, he is apprehensive of the Tarnished, but after they have claimed a Great Rune he becomes willing to share his knowledge of the remaining shardbearers.

In the past, Gideon took in Nepheli Loux after she lost sight of the guidance of Grace, taking advantage of her youthful credulity. He promised her that he would not allow the downtrodden to be cheated any longer if he became Elden Lord. He also became acquainted with Preceptor Seluvis and Dolores the Sleeping Arrow, although he and Seluvis would go their separate ways because of Dolores.

At some point, Gideon engaged in a long exchange with the Two Fingers, and in doing so learned that everything—including the Erdtree and the Two Fingers themselves—had been broken. He also glimpsed into the will of Queen Marika the Eternal, shuddering in fear at an end that should not be. He concluded from this that the queen wished for the Tarnished to struggle eternally.

When a Tarnished champion makes their way to the Roundtable Hold, the first in a long time, Gideon is initially dismissive of them, welcoming them to the Hold but calling them a mere visitor. Gideon encourages the Tarnished to seek a Great Rune in order to gain audience with the Two Fingers and be welcomed as a proper member of the Roundtable Hold.

True to his word, Gideon inducts them as a true member of the Roundtable upon their meeting with the Two Fingers, and shares with them some of the information he has amassed on the Shardbearers.

Although Gideon had amassed knowledge on many of the shardbearers, he had not ascertained the whereabouts of four demigods: Ranni the Witch; Mohg, Lord of Blood; Malenia, Blade of Miquella; and Miquella of the Haligtree. In his search for the latter, he sends his men to ransack the Village of the Albinaurics in Liurnia of the Lakes, knowing that the Albinaurics possess half of a secret medallion that would open the path to the Haligtree. The slaughter of the Albinaurics causes Nepheli to lose faith in him, which causes him to abandon her. He also sought Latenna, an Albinauric woman with knowledge of the location of the other half of the medallion. If the Tarnished claims one half of the medallion, Gideon's underling Ensha will ambush them in Roundtable Hold, apparently of his own volition. After Ensha is defeated, Gideon compensates the Tarnished by sharing the possible whereabouts of the medallion's other half.

When the Erdtree rejects the Tarnished, forcing them to contemplate journeying to the Forge of the Giants to burn the thorns barring entry into the Erdtree, Gideon encourages them to take no heed of the Fingers' warning that this would be a cardinal sin. He also offers to reward the Tarnished for any information they can deliver on the four great runes whose locations are unknown. If the Tarnished pursues this quest to its ending, finding the cocoon of Miquella within the Mohgwyn Dynasty Mausoleum, Gideon thanks them, declaring that this is one of the last pieces he needs to put everything together.

After the Tarnished burns the Erdtree and unseals the Rune of Death, Gideon makes his way to Leyndell, Ashen Capital, where he confronts the Tarnished in the Erdtree Sanctuary. Upon his defeat, he warns them that a Tarnished could not become a Lord, and that a man cannot kill a god.

sections.heading: Character Information
sections.markdown: Sir Gideon Ofnir, the All-Knowing is a boss encounter in Leyndell, Ashen Capital. He utilises both sorceries and incantations in combat, and learns new spells depending on whether you have defeated Rykard, Malenia, or Mohg. He only has seven memory slots, and knows six spells by default, meaning that the spells learned by defeating the aforementioned bosses can replace his default spells. If two of these bosses have been defeated, Gideon will lose Comet Azur. If all three have been defeated, he will lose Triple Rings of Light.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Siofra River** is an underground region in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
One of the two great rivers that flow beneath the Lands Between. Siofra is said to be the grave of civilizations that flourished before the Erdtree, and evidence of this can be found in the many ancient structures that litter the vast, subterranean space. The towering remains of an ancient dynasty are prominent throughout the area, inhabited by the Claymen who once served as the dynasty's priests.

The lower portion of Siofra River can be accessed via the Siofra River Well in Limgrave's Mistwood. This wooded area is home to spectral Ancestral Followers, who live alongside a diverse assortment of wildlife. The remains of a great, horned beast can be found in the Hallowhorn Grounds. Interacting with the remains after lighting the flames scattered throughout the area will facilitate an encounter with an Ancestor Spirit. This area also connects to Caelid via the Deep Siofra Well.

Towering over the woodland is Nokron, one of the Eternal Cities inhabited by the Nox. Nokron is initially inaccessible, however a route is opened when a star falls upon Limgrave, following the defeat of Starscourge Radahn. The Fingerslayer Blade, a treasure of Nokron said to be able to harm the Greater Will and its vassal Fingers, is found within Night's Sacred Ground, beneath a chair-crypt that holds a vast corpse. This upper region also houses another Hallowhorn Grounds, from which the Regal Ancestor Spirit can be encountered. Nearby, the aqueduct hides a coffin which can be used to access Deeproot Depths, guarded by a pair of Valiant Gargoyles.

To the east, on a separate island within the vast cavern, are the ruins of an ancient palace. It is here that Mohg, Lord of Blood has established the seat of his coming Mohgwyn Dynasty, and all the nightmares it may bring.

sections.markdown: Sage Gowry** is a merchant NPC in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Gowry** is an elderly sage dwelling in the blighted Caelid Wilds. When the Empyrean Malenia unleashed the Scarlet Rot during her battle with General Radahn, she permanently blighted Caelid. Since that day, Gowry has dedicated himself to her and the Order of Rot he hopes she will usher in.

Gowry found Millicent and her sisters in the Swamp of Aeonia and raised them as his daughters. Seeing them as buds, he sent each of Millicent's sisters to the Haligtree in the hopes that they would bloom into scarlet valkyries.

Millicent became consumed by the Scarlet Rot, and was housed in a church, where she was worshipped by the Pests. Gowry sought the aid of a Tarnished, offering to reveal to them the secret of the magical town of Sellia in exchange for their aid. Gowry bids the Tarnished to journey deep into the Swamp of Aeonia to retrieve a needle of unalloyed gold, which could stem the effects of the Scarlet Rot. After the Tarnished retrieves the needle, Gowry shares the secret of the town, and asks them for another favor; to find Millicent and give her the needle.

Gowry avoids Millicent when she comes to visit his shack, later telling the Tarnished that she has no need of him anymore, and must embark on her fated journey. The Tarnished may aid Millicent on her journey, even giving her a prosthetic arm. Doing so will earn them Gowry's good will, who will offer to teach them a rot incantation, and reveal to them his allegiance to Malenia.

As Millicent travels to the Haligtree, where Malenia awaits, she draws ever closer to her "sisters", who made the same journey as her. Gowry bids the Tarnished to aid the sisters in murdering Millicent, believing that a betrayal by someone she trusts so dearly will cause her to blossom into a flower, which will be reborn as a scarlet valkyrie when Malenia ascends to godhood.

Should the Tarnished kill Millicent, they will return to Gowry's shack to find him seemingly dead. Should they instead aid Millicent against her sisters, she will prevail, but will remove the golden needle, willfully allowing herself to succumb to the Scarlet Rot. The Tarnished may then find Gowry lamenting Millicent's decision, questioning whether she and Malenia detests him and the other children of rot so utterly.

If the Tarnished attempts to kill Gowry, his body will transform into that of a Kindred of Rot. Upon returning to his shack, he will once again resume his human form, revealing that he can inhabit other pests to avoid death.

sections.markdown: Smithing Master Hewg** is a character in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown: Hewg is a blacksmith at the Roundtable Hold who improves armaments to maximum level and provides other services.

sections.heading: Services
sections.markdown:
- **Strengthen Armament**: Hewg incrementally strengthens weapons up to their maximum levels, but requires Smithing Stones (or Somber Smithing Stones) and Runes to do so.
- **Ashes of War**: Hewg applies Ashes of War and Affinities to weapons.
- **Ash of War Duplication**: Hewg converts Lost Ashes of War into any known Ashes of War.
- **Sell**: Hewg purchases any unwanted items from the player.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
A Scaly Misbegotten bearing aspects of the primordial Crucible, Hewg practiced the once-divine art of smithing. A spirit tuner with distinctive eyes helped him out in the distant past, though she died before he could repay her.

Long ago, Queen Marika cursed Hewg with an impossible task under her Golden Order: to create a weapon capable of slaying a god. Chained to the Roundtable Hold for eternity, he maintained the weapons of Tarnished seeking the Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Game events
sections.markdown:
When he meets Roderika, he recognizes that her eyes share the same hue as those of his old acquaintance. Although reluctant at first, Hewg agrees to take Roderika under his wing at the insistence of the the Tarnished.

After the Tarnished sets fire to the Erdtree, the Roundtable Hold also begins to burn. Hewg's chains are broken, yet he insists on remaining in the hold, where he can continue to smith weapons to slay a god, despite Roderika's pleas for him to leave. As the Roundtable burns, Hewg's mental state deteriorates, causing him to slur his words and, eventually, to forget both Roderika and the Tarnished. Roderika decides to respect Hewg's decision to stay at the Roundtable, and resolves to remain with him. Her last request is for the Tarnished to use the weapons Hewg smithed to slay Queen Marika.

sections.heading: Hewg's Quest
sections.markdown: - Hewg and Roderika's questlines progress together.

sections.heading: Questline progression
sections.markdown:
Smithing Master Hewg remains in a fixed location at the Roundtable Hold throughout the entire game.

1. Speak to Hewg
1. Once Roderika arrives at the Roundtable Hold, speak to Hewg and select the **"About Roderika"** dialogue option.
 - Return to Roderika and tell her what Hewg said.
 - Return to Hewg and select **"About Roderika"** again, followed by **"Would you watch over Roderika?"** and finally **"It's what she wants"**.
 - Reload the area. Roderika moves, seated across from Hewg, now offers spirit tuning services.
1. Upon reaching the Forge of the Giants, return and talk for advice.
1. After burning the Erdtree, return to the Roundtable Hold and select **"Let's talk a while"**. You may then select the dialogue option **"Why are you still making weapons?"**
 - After talking to Roderika and selecting **"About Hewg"**, return to Hewg and select **"What happened to her?"**
1. After defeating the Godskin Duo, return to Roundtable Hold and speak to Hewg and select **"About the god-slaying weapon"**.
1. After defeating Maliketh, the Black Blade, return to Hewg and select **"About yourself"**.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- He wears a brown smith's apron and wields a Hammer.
- Although Hewg shares a model with fellow Scaled Misbegotten, he lacks a tail and hair, but has a beard.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:

- In an early prerelease version of *Elden Ring*, Hewg was found in Stormhill Shack, which at that time served as a character hub. Notably, this is now where Roderika is initially found.
 - Redeemer Guilbert advised the player to meet Hewg, wondering whether he held any unresolved grudges.

Loot: **Can be picked up within the boss arena of Praetor Rykard, just after the fog gate.

This item does not re-spawn when the player has one in either their inventory or chest, even in NG+. However it will re-spawn (and thus can be picked up again) from the same location should the player discard it. This is to make sure that the player always have the means of fighting Rykard with it.

Because of this safeguard it is still possible to obtain duplicates of this weapon:
- **Requirements:**
 - The player needs to not have a copy it in their inventory.
 - Rykard needs to still be alive.
 - The game needs to be in online-mode.
- 1) Stand outside Rykard's arena and attempt to connect to another player's world through any means necessary.
(Tarnished's Furled Finger, Duelist's Furled Finger, Bloody Finger, Recusant Finger, Festering Bloody Finger or Blue Cipher Ring)
- 2) When the game has successfully found a world it can try to connect to, enter Rykard's arena and pick up the Serpent-Hunter before the Loading Screen appears.
- 3) Leave the multiplayer session either by completing your objective or using the Finger Severer.
- 4) When you re-spawn back in your own world, do not fast travel or rest at the Sites of Grace, instead enter Rykard's arena again and you'll see the Serpent Hunter is still there, available to be picked up again for a second time.
(Traveling or resting at the site of grace will make the game check if the Serpent-Hunter is in your inventory before it decides if it'll spawn in a new one for you to pick up)
- It's possible to obtain even more copies of this weapon if the player simply loops back to step 1 after finishing step 3.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown: Wolves are the undying vassals of Empyreans, shadowbound beasts granted by the Two Fingers. Often half-humanoid in appearance, they are tailor-made to reflect their Empyreans and execute their masters' will with unerring loyalty. Should their Empyreans reject the path to godhood presented by the Two Fingers, a terrible curse causes the loyal blades to go mad, becoming dangerous Baleful Shadows.

sections.heading: Maliketh
sections.markdown: The first named Shadowbound Beast is Maliketh, the Black Blade, who became the loyal shadow and half-brother of Queen Marika the Eternal. However, her sole need of her shadow was a vessel to lock away Destined Death, which was harboured in his sword after the defeat of the Gloam-Eyed Queen. After a fragment of the Rune of Death was stolen during the Night of Black Knives he sealed the rune within his own body so that none could steal Death again. When the stolen fragment sprouted in the form of Deathroot throughout the Lands Between, he would attempt to recover it under the alias Gurranq, Beast Clergyman by consuming the Deathroot.

sections.heading: Blaidd
sections.markdown: The other named Shadowbound Beast is Blaidd the Half-Wolf. Blaidd was approved by Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon and given to her daughter, the Empyrean Ranni the Witch, at a young age. He became her stepbrother and they grew up together. In defiance of the fate he was born into, he swore to serve no other master but Ranni, assisting her in her rebellion against the Two Fingers. Against his own will, Blaidd would eventually succumb to becoming a Baleful Shadow, but in his final moments gave himself to Ranni.

sections.heading: Baleful Shadows
sections.markdown: Although all Shadows who turn on their Empyreans are considered Baleful Shadows, there are particular Baleful Shadows that are assassins of the Two Fingers. The last of the Baleful Shadows is killed by the Tarnished in the Ainsel River during Ranni the Witch's quest.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Scarlet Rot** (朱い腐敗, *Akai Fuhai*) is a status effect in *Elden Ring*, inflicting damage over time to the player and serving as a more dangerous variant of the Poison status effect. The player's resistance to this status ailment is determined by their Immunity stat, which is increased by the Vigor stat.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Scarlet Rot is an old legend in the Lands Between, a dangerous sickness that eats away life like a vicious plague. It corrupts men and beasts who come into contact with it, deforming their bodies and eating away their wits, driving them to madness and causing them to act like wild animals. Those afflicted with the Scarlet Rot such as Millicent also suffer from nightmares due to the affliction. Areas afflicted with Scarlet Rot sprout fungal growths or flower buds. As such, Scarlet Rot is often fended off using fire.

The Empyrean and demigod, Malenia, Blade of Miquella harbored the affliction of Scarlet Rot within her body from birth, which has decayed her body and caused her to lose her limbs. Her will, pride, dignity, and sense of self, along with the help of her brother Miquella of the Haligtree's Unalloyed Gold Needle assisted with resisting the call of the Scarlet Rot. However, at the Battle of Aeonia, the final battle of the Shattering, she abandoned this pride to meet Starscourge Radahn's measure. This resulted in the blooming of the first flower of Aeonia causing both Caelid and Radahn to become blighted by the Scarlet Rot. Upon Malenia's return to Miquella's Haligtree, it too was infected and malformed by the Scarlet Rot. The Swamp of Aeonia spawned by the flower in Caelid gave rise to Kindred of Rot, also known as "Pests." Some inorganic beings are capable of contracting and hosting the disease; a number of Crystalians, and their weapons, fester with Scarlet Rot.

Despite the horrific effects of the sickness, some worship the Scarlet Rot as a god. The sickly Maleigh Marais of the Shaded Castle was a private believer, and considered Malenia his personal goddess. To those enraptured by the Scarlet Rot, the mushrooms that spawn from it growing on their bodies are holy vestments that root them to the earth. Long ago, great lords served the Scarlet Rot, perhaps with such large fungal bodies serving as their crowns. Ever since the Battle of Aeonia, Sage Gowry has dedicated himself to the resplendence of the Order of Rot, the cycle of decay and rebirth, desiring Malenia to bloom into a goddess, and her daughters to join her as scarlet valkyries.

Long ago, Malenia's mentor, the Blind Swordsman, sealed away an ancient god that was Rot itself using a flowing sword bestowed upon him by a fairy in legend. The divine essence of this Outer God was sealed in the Lake of Rot in the Ainsel River deep below Liurnia of the Lakes.

The head confessor Crepus, an assassin of the Roundtable Hold serving the Two Fingers, used bolts imbued with Scarlet Rot with his Black-Key Crossbow.

sections.heading: Mechanics
sections.markdown: Scarlet Rot accumulates gradually and comes into effect once the threshold is reached. The higher the player's Immunity stat, the longer it will take for Scarlet Rot to become effective. Immunity can be increased by increasing the Vigor stat. Once effective, the player will receive continual damage over time until the effect wears off.

sections.heading: Skills
sections.markdown: There are currently no skills in the game that apply Scarlet Rot.

sections.heading: Buffs related to Scarlet Rot
sections.markdown: There are certain equipment that gives the player buffs when scarlet rot has been inflicted in the general vicinity, they do not discriminate between what has been poisoned in order to activate, it can be friend, foe and even oneself and generally lasts for around 20 seconds since the last rot infliction.

sections.heading: Swamps
sections.markdown:
Rot swamps can be found in several locations throughout the Lands Between.
They generally comprise of bodies of filthy sludge that continuously build up Scarlet Rot as the player is standing in them. Rolling around in said sludge will also cover the player-character's body with the fluids, which will slowly yet consistently build up Scarlet Rot even if the player is no longer directly standing in the liquid itself or even tries to cure their Rot ailment with boluses. While these stains will gradually wear off over time, they can be removed immediately if it's raining, the player rolls around in clean water or uses Soap.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Sellia, Town of Sorcery** is a location in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
A town in Caelid on the eastern bank of the Swamp of Aeonia.

The Eternal City of Nokron sleeps below Sellia, and it is said that the Sellians are descended from the city's inhabitants. Primeval Sorcerer Lusat, one of the founding Glintstone Sorcerers, came from Sellia. Other Sellian sorcerers followed in Lusat's footsteps, travelling to the Academy of Raya Lucaria to study the Olivinus Conspectus.

Sellian sorcerers are assassins who are said to hunt their fellow sorcerers, employing night sorceries that allowed them to turn their weapons, or their own bodies, invisible to deceive their enemies.

General Radahn studied gravity sorcery in Sellia in his youth, learning from an Alabaster Lord. The knowledge he gained allowed him to challenge the stars during the Starscourge Conflict, where he held the town of Sellia secure.

Presently, the town is inhabited by spectral Glintstone Sorcerers and mechanical marionettes, and many of the buildings have been ensnared by the roots that trail from the nearby Swamp of Aeonia. Several buildings are protected by seals, which can be broken by lighting the flames at the tops of the town's three towers. sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **Shardbearers** (破片の君主, *Hahen no Kunshu*) are special bosses that are key to progression in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown: Defeating a shardbearer grants the player a Great Rune. To progress the story, at least one Great Rune is required to gain an audience with the Two Fingers at the Roundtable Hold, while two are needed to access Leyndell, Royal Capital. Defeating at least three Shardbearers is necessary to achieve an ending.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
The Shardbearers were the inheritors of the Great Runes, the fragments of the Elden Ring, and were primarily among the Demigod offspring of Queen Marika the Eternal. Uniquely among the Shardbearers, Ranni the Witch cast aside her Great Rune. The mad taint of the power they acquired from their Great Runes precipitated the Shattering wherein most of them fought for control of the Lands Between. However, none succeeded in becoming Elden Lord, or the god of a new age.

Unlike the other Shardbearers, Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon, is not a Demigod. She received her Great Rune of the Unborn from Radagon of the Golden Order long before the Shattering. This Great Rune was removed from the Elden Ring long ago and stored within the amber egg that was left by her former husband.

The Tarnished, upon their return to the Lands Between, were tasked by the Two Fingers to defeat the Shardbearers in order to claim their Great Runes, and use them to repair the shattered Elden Ring. Several Tarnished, such as Roundtable Knight Vyke and Sir Gideon Ofnir, the All-Knowing, became shardbearers and earned a personal audience with the Two Fingers.

sections.heading: Facing the Shardbearers
sections.markdown:
Certain bosses or events must be completed before the shardbearers can be fought.
1. Godrick the Grafted (Stormveil Castle, Limgrave):
 - Defeat Margit, the Fell Omen and navigate Stormveil Castle
1. Mohg, Lord of Blood (Mohgwyn Palace, Siofra River):
 - Use the item given by Varre after completing his quest at Rose Church or take the waygate in the Consecrated Snowfield
1. Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon (Academy of Raya Lucaria, Liurnia of the Lakes):
 - Defeat Red Wolf of Radagon and navigate the Academy of Raya Lucaria
1. Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy (Volcano Manor, Mt. Gelmir):
 - Speak to Tanith at the Volcano Manor after completing all three of her contracts, or take the waygate after defeating the Godskin Noble in the Volcano Manor
1. Starscourge Radahn (Redmane Castle, Caelid):
 - Speak to Jerren at Redmane Castle after reaching Altus Plateau or defeating the Crucible Knight & Misbegotten Warrior duo

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- There are several demigods who are not known to be shardbearers. Namely, Godwyn the Golden, Godefroy the Grafted, and the Soulless Demigods carried in the Wandering Mausoleums.
 - Messmer the Impaler is not a shardbearer. He was sent on his crusade and forlorned in the Realm of Shadow prior to Radagon leaving Rennala.
- Radagon was a shardbearer before he gave the amber egg to Rennala.
- The Scadutree Avatar technically becomes a shardbearer after Miquella discards his Great Rune.
- Both Patches and White Mask Varré allude to having gained an audience with the Two Fingers. Similar to other NPCs, they do not drop Great Runes upon defeat.
- Melina receives the Rune of Death in the "Lord of Frenzied Flame" ending if she did not sacrifice herself at the Forge of the Giants.
- Rennala also did not participate in the Shattering due to being locked inside Raya Lucaria Grand Library after the Academy's mages rebelled against the Carian Royals.
 - When the Tarnished confronts Rennala, their battle is interrupted by Ranni the Witch, who conjures a phantom of Rennala in her prime from the amber egg, which the Tarnished defeats instead.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- Localisation Notes
 - In Japanese, the shardbearers are rather called "Monarchs of Fragments" or "Sovereigns of Shards" (破片の君主, *Hahen no Kunshu*.)
 - The Sword Monument that reads "The First Defense of Leyndell / A sovereign alliance rots from within / Traces yet remain of bloody conspiracy" also uses the same kanji 君主 (*Kunshu*) to refer to the "sovereign alliance." This may indicate an alliance between the shardbearers before the First Defense.
 - In English, Enia calls the player a shardbearer after they acquire a Great Rune, however, in Japanese she simply calls them "Master of the/a Great Rune" (大ルーンの主, *Dai Rūn no Omo*.)
 - In English, Tanith refers to the shardbearers vying for power, however, in Japanese she uniquely calls them "Great Rune Monarchs" / "Sovereigns of (the) Great Rune(s)" / (大ルーンの君主, *Dai Rūn no Kunshu*.)

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Young Albinaurics**, also known as **Second-Generation Albinaurics**, are Enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Young Albinaurics are pale, pot-bellied creatures with frog-like faces and large, vacuous, black eyes. Created by human hands, the arcane circumstances of their birth has led many to believe they live impure lives untouched by the Erdtree's grace. Unlike the first generation, the second generation retains the use of their legs at the cost of their ability to speak. Their improved physique allows them to wield a greater variety of weapons, which they use to fight back against the formidable sorcerers that seek to slay them. They revered the ripple and the Crescent Moon.

Some young Albinaurics traveled to the Consecrated Snowfield in search of Miquella's Haligtree. They were imbued with holy energy.

Others followed Miquella to the Mohgwyn Palace, sprouting tangled horns and turning crimson after receiving a boon from the Formless Mother via Mohg's accursed Omen blood. These Sanguine Albinaurics produce bloodthorns whenever they cartwheel, suggesting a link to the blood star. The larger Albinaurics blow into their Curved Great Clubs like alpine horns, summoning the legless Giant Skeletons like the Tibia Mariner in Wyndham Ruins.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.markdown: Regular Albinaurics who freely roam Liurnia of the Lakes, often gathered around the ruins that dot the landscape.

sections.heading: Blessed
sections.markdown: Albinaurics blessed by grace, their once dim eyes now shining with a golden gift. They are capable of casting Discus of Light at foes, and are otherwise unremarkable from their regular variants.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.markdown: Albinaurics tainted by Mohg, Lord of Blood's accursed blood. They roam the swamp surrounding Mohgwyn Palace, ready to defend their Lord from those who would seek to stop the birth of his Dynasty. Those that carry the Great Curved Clubs are able to beckon forth Giant Skeletons. Those that possess lighter weaponry are able to bristle sharpened Bloodthorns of accursed blood from their bodies. Either cart-wheeling into intruders and shredding them to pieces, or painfully expelling them onto their immediate vicinity.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown: - Their frog faces are a reference to the leglessness of other Albinaurics (tadpoles).

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown: - *Albinauric* is a constructed term derived from Latin roots *albus* (pale, white) and ** (gold), suggesting an approximation of silver made from gold.
